chunks: Allah's mercy be upon him said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub said: Ali ibn Muhammad (who elevated the chain) narrated from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Basir, who said: I was sitting before Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and a questioner asked him, saying: May I be your ransom, O son of the Messenger of Allah! How does adversity reach the people of disobedience so that punishment is decreed for them in His Knowledge based on their actions? Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) replied: O questioner, the Knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and High, is that no one from His creation will truly fulfill His right. When He knew this, He bestowed upon His lovers the strength for recognizing Him and removed from them the weightiness of the action based on the reality of what they deserve. And He bestowed upon the people of disobedience the strength for their disobedience due to His prior Knowledge of them, and He did not prevent them from the capacity to accept Him, because His Knowledge is more entitled to the reality of confirmation. So they conformed to what was predestined for them in His Knowledge, even if they were able to do something that would save them from His disobedience. This is the meaning of 'He wills what He wills,' and it is a secret.
ai.seo_question: How does divine knowledge relate to human free will and predestination according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the Shia doctrine of *al-Jabr wa al-Tafwid* (compulsion and delegation) by distinguishing between God's eternal knowledge (*'Ilm*) and the actual bestowal of capacity (*Quwwah*). He explains that God granted His lovers the strength to know Him and relieved them of the burden of deeds, while granting the disobedient the strength to disobey, not by preventing their ability, but because their actions perfectly aligned with His prior knowledge of their reality.
